newsitem.title: USA: SangStat says FDA will review Cyclosporine.
newsitem.headline: SangStat says FDA will review Cyclosporine.

text.p: SangStat Medical Corp on Friday said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has will review the company's formulation of Cyclosporine, an immunosuppressive drug, to determine whether it can be sold.

The Company filed an application for market clearance of its Neoral-bioequivalent form of Cyclosporine on November 27. Neoral is currently being sold by Sandoz AG, and 1995 sales were reported at $1.2 billion worldwide, SangStat said.
Cyclosporine is used in human organ transplants to prevent graft rejection. SangStat has completed five human trials with its cyclosporine formulation in 119 volunteers and patients.

SangStat said the trials showed its form of Cyclosporine was the bioequivalent of the Neoral form in healthy volunteers under both fasted (36 subjects) and fed (21 subjects) conditions. However, the FDA has not yet reviewed these data.
Under current FDA rules, a cyclosporine formulation that is shown to be bioequivalent to Neoral may be approved without the need to duplicate safety and efficacy trials.
If the FDA approves SangStat's CYCLOSPORINE based on bioequivalence to Neoral, SangStat said it intends to market its formulation as a therapeutic substitute for Neoral.
